execution_reference.description: Provider-verified execution reference for this response, when available.

attachments.description:

cursor.description: Opaque channel-bound snapshot watermark, usable as Last-Event-ID.

addressing_bytes.description:
Byte offset into the raw message text (into `args` for a `to` command)

Attachment.description:
One attachment of an activity.

Every fact is what the source declared. Content derived from the bytes
(transcripts, pixels, extracted text) never enters the Activity: the sealed
activity digest covers only what the source reported, and derived content is
produced on demand from the locator.

reference.description:
Stable, non-secret identifier such as `telegram:<file_unique_id>`,
`lark:<key>`, `<platform>:item-<i>` or an owner-supplied value.

oneOf.description:
Where the bytes can be fetched; absent means the attachment is not
retrievable and only its facts are known.
A platform preview from the same native Telegram or Lark message.

AttachmentImage.description: Metadata of one image delivered with the view; never its bytes.

at_ms.description: The frame's position in the video, for keyframes only.

AttachmentImageOrigin.description:
How an image was produced. It is decided per image, because one set of
frames can mix extracted keyframes with a platform thumbnail fallback.

AttachmentSource.description:
Where an attachment's bytes can be fetched.

Locators are non-secret and bound into the activity digest, but they never
carry retrieval authority: the NyxID message ID stays inside the sealed reply
address, and every fetch is authorized by the event_ref that sealed the
activity. Each type is valid only with its matching activity source.

oneOf.description: Exact resource of an authenticated native Lark/Feishu message.
Signed native WhatsApp media; temporary download URLs are never retained.

sha256.description: Canonical lowercase hexadecimal digest from the signed webhook.

oneOf.description: Exact native Discord message attachment; resolved with current bot custody.
Position of the attachment in the NyxID relay callback.
Authenticated embedded Lark/Feishu resource, bound to its source authority revision.
Telegram Bot API file identifiers of a natively received message.
An absolute HTTPS URL supplied by a custom event source.
An RFC 6901 JSON pointer to bytes carried inside the custom event itself.

AttachmentText.description: One page of a transcript or of a document's text.

AttachmentTextSource.description: Where a page of text came from.

AttachmentUnavailableReason.description:

AttachmentView.description: One attachment's facts and the requested view of its content.

detected_type.description: The MIME type sniffed from the bytes, when it was determined.

oneOf.description:

structured_replies.description: Exclusive static structured reply kinds supported for this exact retained event.

thread_history.description: A fixed 20-message prior window is available on explicit request.

received_at.description: Gateway receive timestamp, persisted before provider launch.

source_occurred_at.description: Explicit CloudEvent time; absent when the source did not report one.

ChannelCreateRequest.description:
Request wrapper used by channel creation.
Top-level `routing` is not accepted. After creation, configure routing with
`PUT /v1/channels/{channel_id}/routing` and `{expected_version,routing}`.

durable_custom_execution.description: Immutable opt-in to durable execution for this channel's Custom source.

ChannelCreation.description: Retained management admission, independent of process-local idempotency caches.

ChannelId.description: An encrypted pointer to a CMA channel record.

ChannelListItem.description: An owner-visible record whose original channel ID may predate recoverable creation.

version.description: Storage version of this read; does not authorize a mutation or retry.

thread_contract_versions.description: Explicit opt-in support; absent/empty means unsupported.

ChannelUpdateRequest.description:
Update body; credentials are retained when this field is absent.
Top-level `routing` is not accepted; full updates preserve the saved policy.
Use `PUT /v1/channels/{channel_id}/routing` to change routing.

durable_custom_execution.description: Optional echo for older clients; a supplied value must match the saved mode.

index.description: Zero-based position in the rendered text, not a delivery retry counter.

Consumer.description:
An additional consumer of a channel, beside the implicit `default`. It
carries its own binding, profile and agent key, so it is stored whole;
a channel holds at most seven.

Every optional field is omitted when absent or at its default, so a
stored consumer keeps its bytes when read and written back.

agent_key_hash.description: The public hash of the consumer's agent key, `sha256:<64 hex>`.

label.description: 1..=64 printable characters for reply labels; absent means `name`.

mentionable.description: Whether a leading `@name` or `/to name` may address it.

non_human.description:
Whether this consumer answers non-human actors (custom events and
hand-offs). Absent means its provider slug is configured as non-human.

pending.description: Stored before its provider binding exists; never routed.

ConsumerId.description:
A channel consumer's stable identifier: "default" or "csm_" + 12 lowercase hex.
Assigned by the gateway and never reused within a channel.

The grammar admits no `\x1f`, the separator of the gateway's identity
derivations, so an identifier can be joined into one unambiguously.

ConsumerName.description:
A consumer's chat name, `^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{1,31}$`, unique per channel.
Names are lowercase, so comparing two of them is exact.

Reserved: `all`, `everyone`, `here`, `to`, any `csm_` prefix, and
`default`, which only the default consumer may use. The grammar is a
property of the type; the reserved words are refused by the channel
readers, which know whether a name belongs to the default consumer and
can point at the offending field.

ConsumerReply.description: A consumer's own reply policy, overriding the channel's.

ConsumerSummary.description: Which of a routed channel's consumers a context response was read for.

label.description: The consumer's reply label, else its name.

oneOf.description:
The consumer the calling agent key belongs to; present only on a
channel with routing, so an unrouted response keeps its bytes.
Reaction-only reference to an exact retained native user message.
Explicitly requested current text context of the original native thread.

before_message_id.description: Original/last scanned pre-cutoff ID. Native provider scan position remains in the cursor.

fetched_at.description: Gateway fetch time, not a platform snapshot timestamp.

messages.description: Chronological within the page; continuation travels backward.

omitted_message_count.description: Scanned rows omitted by cutoff, deletion, unsupported content or actor policy.

scanned_messages.description: Raw rows scanned, including native thread rows at/after the original timestamp.

auto_archive_duration.description: Required Discord minutes: 60, 1440, 4320, or 10080. Omit for Telegram.

CustomAttachments.description: Where a custom event lists its attachments and which origins they may name.

origins.description:
Exact HTTPS origins (`https://host[:port]`) an item URL may name. Empty
admits only inline `data:` items.

pointer.description: RFC 6901 pointer, relative to the event's `data`, at an array of items.

DefaultConsumer.description:
The presentation and policy of the `default` consumer. Its binding,
profile and agent key stay in the definition's top-level fields, so its
storage, conversation ids and tokens never change when routing is added.

label.description: 1..=64 printable characters for reply labels; absent means `name`.

mentionable.description: Whether a leading `@name` or `/to name` may address it.

non_human.description: Whether it answers non-human actors; absent means by provider slug.

DefaultReply.description:
The channel's default reply destination. Routed preparation pins its exact
nonsecret address; sends require the current definition to still authorize
that address and resolve credentials separately.

oneOf.description: A chat of the native Telegram source.

The channel's result webhook sinks.

native_lark_webhook_url.description: Configure only on a separately provisioned native app. Never replace a NyxID callback.

EventAttestationRequest.description:
All identifiers are comparisons against the capability's original target.
This cannot select another target, attachment or filesystem path.

oneOf.description:
Required by attachment and supplement admission. An event-only result
does not attest file bytes or derived text.

binding_generation.description:
The generation actually present in the frozen Gateway request. None is
not a claim about Manager generation; Manager must check its own parent.

Exact sealed capability expiry, as Unix seconds. This comparison lets
Manager bound a deferred continuation without trusting caller expiry.

queue_lifetime_seconds.description: Binding message queue lifetime; omitted uses 300 seconds, maximum 86400.

oneOf.description: More provider rows remain to scan; native thread pages may contain no earlier messages.

current_summaries.description: Summaries may advance during paging; intermediate transitions are not archived.

parts.description: Concatenate decoded parts in index order, then deserialize ChannelActivity.

history_event_id.description: Opaque identity used by the details route; activity.event_id is the source identity.

downloads.description: The binding may save originals into its workspace.

transcripts.description: Audio and video can be transcribed.

message_parts.description:

An unknown aggregate outcome can retain confirmed earlier parts.

LarkMessageEffectsBinding.description: Separate owner opt-in for effects on exact confirmed CMA outbound messages.

app_id.description: Receiving app from the independently configured relay bot.

user_service_id.description: Exact allowed NyxID UserService; never a provider credential.

name.description: Required only for rename: 1–100 printable characters. Omit for every other action.

retirement_expected_version.description: Expected version for the retained Delete intent of a retired incomplete channel.

MediaArtifactClaim.description:
The descriptor always names the original uploaded file. For a derived kind,
content_sha256 hashes exact UTF-8 derived text; source_sha256 hashes the bytes
consumed by derivation. For Original both hashes name the original bytes.

text_sha256.description:
None for an upload; required for a queued supplement. Hashes the complete
canonical input, including the Manager-verified persisted file path.

MediaAuthorization.description:
The structured header credential for a ready download. The token is
scoped to one event attachment and is single-use; it is never logged.

MediaControlsCapabilities.description: Exact media/control combination supported for this event's verified destination.

clear_media.description: Explicit clear_native_attachments removes every upload on a confirmed card.

kinds.description: Exact attachment kinds supported with controls; absent means the parent kinds apply.

replace_media.description: Replace the supported upload set on the same durable card through a confirmed PATCH.

MediaDownload.description:
A ready download: one `curl` command and a structured authorization header
that work once and expire at `expires_at`. The URL never carries the link.

authorization.description: The structured credential for clients that cannot execute shell text.

curl.description:
The command to run once in the agent's workspace; its
`Authorization` header carries the same link as `authorization`.

expires_at.description: Unix seconds after which the link is refused.

MediaVariant.description: The platform's own name for the media, finer than `AttachmentKind`.

scope.description: Exact bot-message or received-user-message authority; never arbitrary IDs.

reaction.description: Empty clears the bot's reaction; the gateway supports at most one.

get.description: Bounded recent activity. Actor id is always redacted and display_name is a fixed role label (Participant, Bot, System, or Actor not reported); kind is preserved. This presentation copy is not canonical input for routing or replay. Event identity, cursor, timestamps and consumer/delivery state are preserved.

SSE activity/reset events contain complete ActivityPage snapshots, including on every connection. Actor id is always redacted and display_name is a fixed role label (Participant, Bot, System, or Actor not reported); kind is preserved. This presentation copy is not canonical input for routing or replay. Apply each snapshot atomically. id is an opaque cursor; reconnect with Last-Event-ID or cursor. reset means the cursor predates retained activity. This is recent bounded activity, not a complete audit log.
